paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when it came time to save, God did not wait for help. He says, "I looked, but there was no one to help; I was appalled that no one assisted. So My arm brought Me salvation…" (Isaiah 63:5). The One coming from Edom is "mighty to save" (Isaiah 63:1), and the saving was never riding on anybody else showing up.

Now, I'll be honest, this passage is heavy. It talks about a day of vengeance, and I think that's a part we don't rush past. But look at what else sits in the same heart: "the year of My redemption had come" (Isaiah 63:4). Vengeance and redemption show up side by side, so this is a God who deals with evil and saves His people, and He does both on purpose.

So what does that mean for you? It means your rescue doesn't hang on how strong you are, how ready you are, or whether anybody else came through. I spent years in a drawer waiting on somebody to remember me, and it was the Most High who came and got me. Rest in the One who is mighty to save, and let that be the thing you stand on today, baker. This is one of Isaiah's messages, and I'm already excited to see where the prophets take us next.
